chain.basis: BIS names advanced computing items, including AI chips and servers, and the other item categories; it does not describe them in terms of a supply chain. The placement is the curator's reading of those categories.
chain.placement: Advanced computing at the end of the chain: finished AI chips and servers received in the UAE. Most of the release concerns items outside the semiconductor chain (military items, satellites and spacecraft, and dual-use items for energy and water); it does not concern chip design, chip fabrication or chipmaking equipment.

facts.text: Two rules were announced; BIS says they restrict the PRC’s ability to obtain advanced computing chips, develop and maintain supercomputers, and manufacture advanced semiconductors.

The rule takes effect in phases after filing for Public Inspection with the Federal Register: the semiconductor manufacturing items restrictions on filing (October 7, 2022), the U.S.-person restrictions five days later (October 12, 2022), and the advanced computing and supercomputer controls and the rule’s other changes 14 days later (October 21, 2022).

comparison.text: The October 2022 release announced two rules restricting the PRC's ability to obtain advanced computing chips and to manufacture advanced semiconductors, effective in phases. This release moves the other way for one destination: it eases controls for the UAE and approves license-free receipt of advanced computing items, and it states no effective date. Both are announcements as of their dates, not current rules.
comparison.title: Commerce restricts advanced computing and chipmaking items for the PRC

readout.text: A change of the UAE's Country Groups under the Export Administration Regulations: BIS will remove it from Groups D:3 and D:4 and reclassify it as Group A:5.
Eligibility for License Exception Strategic Trade Authorization: license-free exports, reexports and in-country transfers for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities.
A Commerce approval for the UAE Government and certain companies to receive advanced computing items in the UAE license-free, including AI chips and servers.
The regulatory text: the release says a Federal Register notice implements the changes it describes.

Items under the exception: Commerce-controlled military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; dual-use items useful in oil and gas production, desalination and civil nuclear power generation; and other items available to Country Group A:5 destinations license-free.
Which companies are approved to receive advanced computing items, how they are approved, and any limit on quantities or end uses.
Announced on July 10, 2026, as changes BIS will make; the Federal Register notice is described as available for public inspection.
An effective date for any of the changes, or the date of the notice's publication.

Reasons given for the special status: the UAE's status as a U.S. Major Defense Partner, the military partnership, and its commitment to preventing the diversion and misuse of sensitive U.S. technology.

The advanced-computing approval is described as consistent with the U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework signed in May 2025, under which the UAE reaffirmed its investment commitments, including matching investments in U.S. AI digital infrastructure buildout.
Any condition attached to the new status or to the approvals, or what would follow if the commitments were not kept.
